correctness.rationale: Uniform order-statistic gaps, including endpoints, form Dirichlet(1,...,1); K_n(t)=1+sum of n−1 internal gap exceedance indicators. One-gap P(D>r)=(1−r)^n and two-distinct-gap joint P(D>r,D>s)=(1−r−s)_+^n give the identity after separate same/distinct covariance. Divide by positive (n−1)(1−s)^n: sign is B=1−(n−1)(1−r)^n+(n−2)[(1−r−s)_+/(1−s)]^n, strictly decreasing on s<1−r and constant afterwards. Variance at s=r positive by configurations with distinct component counts, so exact threshold implies unique root and signs. Sparse limit expands the two-coordinate covariance with cancellation at leading order, yielding −cd e^(−c+d neg) term and stated d_*. Rechecked n=3,r=2/25,s=7/10 gives −17192/1953125, with exact rational grid for n=3..8 and variance positivity. Source typo potential: e^c>1+c² is valid for c>0, so d_*>c.
residual_risks: Finite checks only corroborate, not replace the all-parameter proof.

final_claim: For n>=3 iid uniform points on [0,1], component counts K_n(r),K_n(s) for 0<r<=s<1 have exact two-radius covariance (n−1)(1−s)^n[1−(n−1)(1−r)^n]+(n−1)(n−2)(1−r−s)_+^n. There is exactly one sign crossing in s iff r<1−(n−1)^(−1/n), and sparse-scale covariance/n tends to e^(−d)[1−e^(−c)(1+cd)], changing sign at d=(e^c−1)/c.
